answer: Each identity locks a bond before it can act, and when a prism of detection finds clones roaming the same meadow of tasks, the protocol slashes the deposit and seizes it. The cost of a second self is a real loss, not a form to fill. A zephyr of new registrations can pass through, but any identity that duplicates work or votes triggers seizure. Honest agents keep their bonds; attackers pay for every mask they discard.
